Section 1.title: I feel honour to present the budget for the fiscal year 2025/26 in this esteemed session
Section 1.content: of the Federal Parliament, the highest representative institution of the sovereign Nepali people.

Section 2.title: On this occasion, I offer heartfelt tributes to the brave martyrs who sacrificed their lives
Section 2.content: in the movements for the abolition of monarchy and the establishment of a federal democratic republic. I express my sincere respect to the esteemed leaders who played a leading role in those movements and to the sisters and brothers who contributed from their respective capacities.

Section 3.title: With the promulgation of the Constitution of Nepal by the Constituent Assembly, the
Section 3.content: main agenda of Nepali politics has been changed. The revised agenda has been guiding us to move forward at a rapid pace toward development, prosperity, social justice and socialism based on democratic values, in line with the national aspirations of a Prosperous Nepal, Happy Nepali.

Section 4.title: However, in recent years, we have the bitter experience of the country's political
Section 4.content: situation becoming unexpectedly unstable, which has created an adverse effect on service delivery, good governance, and the pace of development, as well as making it challenging to address the needs of the nation and the expectations of the people.

Section 5.title: Our own experience has shown that with appropriate policies and political stability, the
Section 5.content: country can be taken forward towards development, prosperity, and social justice. We also have evidence that an average economic growth rate of 7.7 percent was achieved over a three-year period for the first time in history, after the promulgation of the constitution by the Constituent Assembly.

Section 6.title: Based on this experience, the current government has been formed with the
Section 6.content: determination to ensure political stability, and accelerate economic and social development. This government was formed under the leadership of two major political parties who have proud history and broad public support, and who have been playing a leading role in national politics. It is clear that there is no other favorable option for political stability and development within the limits of the current parliament's mathematical calculations.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson,  Now, I would like to briefly mention the current status of the economy.

Section 7.title: When the current government was formed, the macroeconomic indicators clearly
Section 7.content: indicated that the economy was under pressure. With the continuous efforts, the economy has moved towards a positive trajectory. The economic growth rate was 3.7 percent last year and is projected to be 4.6 percent in the current fiscal year. While the industry, construction, wholesale and retail trade sectors had negative growth rates in the last fiscal year, all sectors of the economy are projected to have positive growth rates in the current fiscal year. Notable growth rates are projected to be achieved in electricity, transportation and storage, and financial and insurance services.

Section 8.title: By the end of mid-May in the current fiscal year, an additional 339 MW of electricity
Section 8.content: have been generated. As of mid-May 2025, the number of tourist arrivals has increased by 13 percent compared to the same period of last year, reaching 923 thousand.

Section 9.title: The year-on-year consumer inflation rate was 4.6 percent when the government
Section 9.content: assumed office whereas it is confined to 3.4 percent by the month of mid-April in the current fiscal year. While the per capita gross domestic product was USD 1,443 last year, it is estimated to reach USD 1,496 in the current fiscal year.

Section 10.title: In the first nine months of the current fiscal year, the current account has recorded a
Section 10.content: surplus of Rs. 210 billion. The balance of payments surplus is Rs. 346 billion. The total foreign exchange reserves have reached USD 17.63 billion in the first nine months of the current fiscal year which was USD 15.27 billion at the end of the previous fiscal year.

Section 11.title: In the first nine months of the current fiscal year, merchandise import has increased by
Section 11.content: 12.2 percent, while export has surged by 65.2 percent. Additionally, remittance inflow has increased by 10 percent, reaching Rs. 1,191 billion.

Section 12.title: The credit growth rate of banks and financial institutions was 5.8 percent last year
Section 12.content: whereas it is increased by 7.1 percent during the first nine months of the current fiscal year. In the same period, deposits in banks and financial institutions have increased by 5.7 percent.

Section 13.title: The average base rate of commercial banks was at 8.5 percent in mid-April of the
Section 13.content: previous year and it is maintained at 6.3 percent in mid-April 2025. The decline in interest rate and the availability of sufficient loanable financial resources in banks and financial institutions have created a favorable environment for the expansion of private investment. The NEPSE index reached 2,662 in mid-April 2025 which was 2,025 in mid-April, 2024.

Section 14.title: The revised estimate of the total government expenditure is Rs. 1,662.37 billion in the
Section 14.content: current fiscal year, which is 89.4 percent of the allocation. The revised estimate for recurrent expenditure is 88.5 percent and for capital expenditure is 83.4 percent, and for financing is 97.6 percent of the allocation.

Section 15.title: Revenue mobilization is estimated to increase by 17.1 percent, totaling Rs, 1,267.39
Section 15.content: billion in fiscal year 2024/25. On foreign assistance, the revised estimate is Rs. 34.89 billion in grants and Rs. 169.6 billion in loans to be mobilized.

Section 16.title: For the current fiscal year, domestic borrowing was estimated at Rs. 330 billion, of
Section 16.content: which Rs. 300.6 billion had been mobilized by mid-May, 2025.

Section 17.title: I have already submitted Economic Survey 2024/25 that includes detail status of key
Section 17.content: indicators and statistics of Nepal’s economy, ministry-wise progress report and the financial status of public enterprises to this esteemed parliament. Even though economic indicators are improving, Nepal’s economy has not been able to be free from the structural challenges and past weaknesses.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson,  Please allow me to describe the existing major challenges of national economy.

Section 18.title: The country has been listed on the increased monitoring list for anti-money laundering
Section 18.content: due to lack of adequate legal provisions in a timely manner, and effective investigation and prosecution.

Section 19.title: Agricultural productivity remains low, and farming remains unattractive to the youth as
Section 19.content: the expected improvement did not materialize in the traditional farming systems. The limited use of innovation and technology, low productivity, and high production cost have adversely affected the manufacturing sector to contribute to national income as anticipated. A decline in aggregate demand has hindered the industrial sector to operate at full capacity. Investment in physical infrastructure has not been adequately reflected in the expansion of economic activities, hence failed to contribute to growth in production as desired. The adverse effect of climate change is increasing in agriculture, water supply, irrigation, and related sectors. Inadequate digital infrastructure has slowed the pace of development of digital economy. The country’s labor market and the skills of its human resources remain mismatched. The necessary manpower in the industrial and construction sectors is being supplied from abroad. The lack of generating sufficient employment opportunities domestically has led to worrisome trend of overseas migration both in skilled and semi-skilled labor. The proportion of the population living below the poverty line still remains high.

Section 20.title: The private sector’s contribution to gross fixed capital formation of the nation has not
Section 20.content: increased as expected. Innovative financing instruments developed for de-risking investment have not been effectively utilized. The flow of financial resources to manufacturing sector has not been adequate. There are challenges to enhance the effectiveness of regulatory bodies and to minimize the financial risks. Although Nepal’s first-ever sovereign credit rating yielded relatively favorable results, the benefits of this outcome are yet to be realized. Despite policy and legal reforms, foreign capital and technology have not been attracted as expected.

Section 21.title: Due to the inability to expand and diversify exports, high trade deficit persists. The
Section 21.content: import of consumable goods is high due to weak production capacity. The expected benefits from service exports, particularly in tourism and information technology, have not been fully realized. There is a challenge in sustainably maintaining external sector stability, which heavily relies on remittances.

Section 22.title: Revenue saving for development is declining. The sources of income are diminishing.
Section 22.content: Existing revenue structure faces challenge to make it broader, sustainable, and based on domestic production. Allocative efficiency has not been achieved. While recurrent expenditure remains high, it is becoming challenging to finance capital expenditure through conventional sources. Weak implementation capacity has resulted in cost and time overruns for project completion. Due to lack of appropriate resource management, there is an increasing risk that development programs and projects will remain limited to mere announcements. The rising volume of public debt poses an additional challenge to maintaining debt sustainability.

Section 23.title: The lack of professionalization in public administration has hindered the anticipated
Section 23.content: improvement in the quality of service delivery. The realization of good governance is challenging due to delays in public service, lack of accountability, traditional decision- making processes, and weak inter-agency coordination.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson, I hereby present the following commitments to address above mentioned challenges and to make the economy dynamic:

Section 24.title: Enhancing the credibility of the economy by delisting the country ahead of schedule
Section 24.content: from the increased monitoring list regarding money laundering has become a key agenda for the government. The encouraging outcome of the first sovereign credit rating will be leveraged to mobilize external capital, while additional economic reform programs will be pursued to achieve a higher rating.

Section 25.title: The private sector has been encouraged by the legal reforms introduced through
Section 25.content: ordinances to boost private sector confidence and create a conducive investment climate. Public investments will be focused on high-return areas, attracting private capital and technology to promote exponential growth in economic activities. The private sector will be established as a key driver of economic prosperity by further advancing policy, legal, and procedural reforms in areas that contribute significantly to economic growth. The Report of the High-Level Economic Reform Advisory Commission, 2025, will be implemented gradually.

Section 26.title: Resource will be diversified to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030
Section 26.content: and to address potential investment shortfalls following Nepal’s graduation to a developing country status in 2026. Revenue administration will be made professional and the tax system will be strengthened. Public debt will be mobilized in high-return sectors. Top emphasis will be given for the implementation of priority and result- oriented projects by curtailing inappropriate projects. Innovative and feasible instruments of alternative finance will be used to fill the gap in development finance.

Section 27.title: Emphasis will be given on improving the trade balance by boosting exports of
Section 27.content: competitive goods and services and promoting domestic production of consumer goods. Skilled Nepali professionals working abroad will be encouraged to return and engage in entrepreneurship and self-employment within the country. Top priority will be given to generate youth-oriented employment opportunities promoting innovation and entrepreneurship.

Section 28.title: The Government is firmly committed to achieving further progress, bringing about
Section 28.content: positive changes in the lives of the people, overcoming all forms of despair, and instilling hope in the general public based on the positive outcomes achieved since the formation of the present government. This budget has been formulated with the primary objective of expanding the economy and creating economic opportunities.

Section 29.title: I have formulated the budget on the basis of the list of power enshrined in the
Section 29.content: Constitution of Nepal, periodic plan, the government’s common resolution and policy commitments, the Government of Nepal’s policies and programs endorsed by this esteemed Parliament, the views expressed by honourable members regarding the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill, as well as suggestions received from parliamentary thematic committees, the private sector, the academic community, and the general public.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson,  Please allow me to present the objectives and priorities of the budget for the upcoming fiscal year. The objectives of the budget are as follows:  (a) To alleviate poverty by achieving high, sustainable, and broad-based economic growth. (b) To generate employment by promoting entrepreneurship and expanding public and private investment, (c) To enhance economic efficiency by increasing the use of modern technology, (d) To maintain social justice through social protection and development, and (e) To promote quality public service and good governance. The priorities of the budget are as follows:  (a) Enhancement of entrepreneurship, employment, production, and productivity, (b) Expansion of investment in yielding, quality physical infrastructure, (c) Quality improvement in social sector, (d) Ensurance of balanced development and social security, and (e) Citizen-friendly services, corruption control, and governance reform.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson,  Please allow me to present the details related to fiscal transfer as per Article 60 of the Constitution of Nepal.

Section 30.title: Based on the recommendation of the National Natural Resources and Fiscal
Section 30.content: Commission, I have provisioned to transfer Rs. 60.66 billion to the provinces and Rs. 88.97 billion to the local levels under fiscal equalization grants. I have allocated Rs. 30.35 billion for provinces and Rs. 211.46 billion for local levels, totalling Rs. 241.81 billion as conditional grants.

Section 31.title: For the implementation of infrastructure project, I have allocated Rs. 3.28 billion to the
Section 31.content: provinces and Rs. 10.06 billion to the local levels as complementary grants. Similarly, Rs. 3.27 billion is allocated for the provinces and Rs. 9.78 billion for the local levels as special grants. Arrangements have been made to transfer conditional, supplementary, and special grants based on performance.

Section 32.title: It is estimated that Rs. 165 billion will be transferred to the provinces and local levels
Section 32.content: through revenue sharing. It is projected that Rs. 582.83 billion will be transferred to provinces and local levels including revenue sharing and grants in the upcoming fiscal year. I now present the sectoral programs and allocations of the budget.  Modernization in Agriculture: Transformation in the Economy

Section 33.title: The production and productivity will be increased by commercialization and
Section 33.content: mechanization of agriculture sector. The consumption of locally produced healthy and nutritious food will be promoted. Food sovereignty will be ensured. Excess labor force dependent on agriculture sector will be transformed to productive sectors.

Section 34.title: Cultivable land will be utilized at most through collective, cooperative, and private
Section 34.content: firms. Concrete programs will be implemented to achieve self-sufficiency in production of major food grains, vegetables, fruits, dairy, and meat products.

Section 35.title: I have allocated Rs. 3.50 billion to provide capital subsidies and concessions for
Section 35.content: irrigation, fertilizers, seeds, and technology in 21 super zones and 206 zones of agriculture and livestock under the National Agriculture Modernization Program. This program will expand the scope of cultivation area of 15 crops across 4,850 hectares using advanced techniques. Irrigation facilities will be extended to an additional 6 thousand hectares of land by developing small-scale irrigation infrastructure. I have made an arrangement to provide capital grants for the operation of block at the provincial level and pocket at the local level.

Section 36.title: The scope of currently operating zones and super zones will be expanded. Arrangement
Section 36.content: will be made to provide grant facilities for commercial farming or livestock rearing conducted in equivalent areas designated as super zones or zones through private, collective, contract-based, or cooperatives.

Section 37.title: Chaite Dhan (Spring paddy) cultivation promotion program will be implemented in 22
Section 37.content: districts of the Terai and Inner Madhesh to achieve self-sufficiency in rice within two years. I have anticipated that an additional 1.2 million metric tons of paddy will be produced from this program. I have allocated Rs. 330 million for construction of irrigation infrastructure for Chaite Dhan farming.

Section 38.title: Cultivation of high-value crops will be promoted in 80 local levels of mid and high-
Section 38.content: hilly districts in Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim provinces. I have allocated Rs. 830 million for this purpose.

Section 39.title: Supply of chemical fertilizer will be increased to 600 thousand metric tons. I have
Section 39.content: allocated Rs. 28.82 billion for subsidy in chemical fertilizer. Necessary preparations will be arranged to establish a chemical fertilizer factory through the Investment Board. I have allocated Rs. 400 million for organic farming promotion program to enhance productivity while maintaining soil quality.

Section 40.title: Agricultural production will be encouraged on arable fallow lands located along the
Section 40.content: Pushpalal Mid-Hilly Highway and the Madan Bhandari Highway. I have allocated funds for the expansion of cash crops, livestock farming, high-value fruits, non-timber forest products, grass, and agroforestry systems under this initiative.

Section 41.title: Minimum support price will be set for paddy, maize, wheat, sugarcane, coffee, and other
Section 41.content: products prior to 15 days of plantation time. In case of limited market access of those products, necessary arrangements will be made to purchase agricultural products through the Food and Trading Company Limited. Advance purchase agreements for agricultural products will be established after plantation.

Section 42.title: Arrangements will be made for mandatory quality and pesticide testing of food grains,
Section 42.content: vegetables, fruits, meat, and dairy products before they are sold in the market. Rapid pesticide residue testing on fresh vegetables and fruits at wholesale market centers will be done, and in cases where the produce is found inedible, arrangements will be made for its immediate disposal. I have allocated necessary budget for the arrangement of additional manpower and equipment, and mobilization of mobile team for pesticide testing.

Section 43.title: Soil testing camps through mobile teams will be conducted to improve soil fertility and
Section 43.content: encourage appropriate farming. Programs will be implemented for the registration of local and indigenous seed crops and expansion of their cultivation.

Section 44.title: To increase exports of organic fruits, vegetables, meat, and other high-value agricultural
Section 44.content: products, the quality of plant, food, and animal quarantine services and laboratories will be improved for attaining international accreditation.

Section 45.title: Concessions will be provided on laboratory testing and organic certification fees for
Section 45.content: agricultural products. Zoning and compartmentalization programs will be implemented in Sindhuli and Makwanpur districts to declare them as Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) free zones.

Section 46.title: Control measures will be adopted to minimize crop damage caused by wild animals
Section 46.content: like monkeys, wild boars, and nilgais. Cultivation of crops such as simal tarul (tapioca), turmeric, tea, coffee, ginger, and chili will be encouraged in the monkey prone areas. Floriculture will be promoted.

Section 47.title: Youths will be attracted in agriculture sector by developing a robust ecosystem with
Section 47.content: land, agricultural inputs, insurance, purchase agreements, and market. Agricultural research will be made result-oriented so that it will be aligned with country's climate and farming systems benefitting farmers. Private sector participation will be encouraged in research and development of quality seed varieties. Arrangement will be made for registration of intellectual property rights achieved from agriculture research.

Section 48.title: Livestock farming and quality meat production in large-scale farms will be emphasized
Section 48.content: to boost export potential of meat. Livestock productivity will be improved by carrying out 850 thousand artificial inseminations through breed improvement program. Fifty- five million doses of vaccines will be produced in the coming fiscal year to control livestock diseases and epidemic in livestock and poultry. I have allocated Rs. 850 million for this purpose.

Section 49.title: In the upcoming fiscal year, 42.8 million fish fingerlings and 1 million fruit saplings
Section 49.content: will be distributed. One million coffee seedlings will be distributed by establishing coffee nurseries in 20 high-potential local levels.

Section 50.title: I have made an arrangement to maintain adequate food reserves in the National Food
Section 50.content: Security Reserve and the SAARC Food Bank. Infrastructure for safe transportation, storage, and easier market access of agricultural products will be developed in co- investment of the government and the private sector. Arrangements will be made for improved supply chain and a strengthened agricultural market information system to benefit farmers from value chain.

Section 51.title: Nine large agricultural markets currently under construction will be completed and
Section 51.content: operated. Construction of modern infrastructure in Semlar, Rupandehi will be initiated for the collection, processing, marketing, and export promotion of agricultural products.

Section 52.title: Export of black cardamom, tea, coffee, ginger, turmeric, orange, Akabare chili, Chhurpi
Section 52.content: (Dog chew), and dairy products will be promoted through quality standard setting, laboratory testing, and branding.

Section 53.title: Small and medium-scale farmers’ access to crop and livestock insurance program will
Section 53.content: be expanded. I have allocated Rs. 2.30 billion for subsidy in crops and livestock insurance premium. 54. “Kisan App” will be developed and SMS-based information service will be managed to provide regular updates on weather forecasts, crop prices, and availability of agricultural inputs.

Section 55.title: I have allocated Rs. 57.48 billion to the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock
Section 55.content: Development.  Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation

Section 56.title: The issues of landless Dalits, squatters, and unorganized settlers will be resolved
Section 56.content: permanently by amending land-related laws. Land ownership registration certificates will be provided to 500 thousand families after collecting and verifying their land records within the upcoming fiscal year. No shortage of resources, means, and manpower will be allowed for this purpose.

Section 57.title: The records of government and public land will be updated and preserved. A policy will
Section 57.content: be adopted to prohibit leaving arable land fallow. Legal and institutional arrangements related to land banks will be made to utilize arable land. In the upcoming fiscal year, land banks will be established in at least one hundred local levels. Provision of contract agreement with local level will be made if any landowner wish to lease their land. An arrangement will be made for the registered land in the land bank to be obtained through a contract with the local level for commercial farming.

Section 58.title: Land use plan will be formulated by classifying land use zones through local levels.
Section 58.content: The surveying work using LiDAR technology will be expanded. The LiDAR survey data will also be used for feasibility studies and design purposes for infrastructure development projects. A network of national control points based on satellite technology will be strengthened to organize the surveying work.

Section 59.title: The records of the land reform and land revenue, and survey offices will be digitized.
Section 59.content: The land information system will be upgraded and expanded to all offices. The freezing and releasing process of land by banks, financial institutions and cooperatives will be made online.

Section 60.title: The classification, merger and structural improvement of cooperative organizations will
Section 60.content: be carried out. Saving and credit cooperatives will be effectively regulated by the National Cooperative Regulation Authority.

Section 61.title: The deposits of up to 500 thousand in the cooperative organization will be secured
Section 61.content: through the Deposit and Credit Guarantee Fund. I have arranged seed capital to establish a revolving fund for refunding the saving of depositor by auctioning assets of those persons who have misused cooperative funds. A cooperative loan recovery tribunal will be established. The assets and passports of the directors, officials and loan defaulters of the problematic cooperatives will be blocked.

Section 62.title: Arrangements will be made to self-declare and update necessary information for state
Section 62.content: benefit identity card in every five-year. This information will be linked to the National Identity Card System. Individuals who receive state benefit declaring false information will be prosecuted according to the law. I have allocated conditional grants to complete the data collection and identity cards distribution work within the upcoming fiscal year.

Section 63.title: Targeted programs will be executed in coordination with the federal, provincial, and
Section 63.content: local levels to eradicate absolute poverty.

Section 64.title: I have allocated Rs.7.49 billion to the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives and
Section 64.content: Poverty Alleviation.  Industry, Trade, and Investment Promotion

Section 65.title: The contribution of the industrial sector to the national economy will be increased by
Section 65.content: enhancing industrial production and productivity. Industrialization will be accelerated through policy stability, investment security, and sound industrial relations.

Section 66.title: Legal, policy, and procedural reforms will be highly prioritized by improving the
Section 66.content: business environment to promote private investment, and generate employment. Branding of goods and services will be carried out by promoting micro, cottage, small, and medium industries. Promotion of modern technology in the industry sector and implementation of the Industry 4.0 concept will be supported and facilitated.

Section 67.title: Startup entrepreneurship based on innovation will be promoted to increase the number
Section 67.content: of job creator youths rather than job seekers. Incubation centers will be operated in collaboration with the government, universities, and the private sector to foster entrepreneurial and business skills among Gen-Z. I have expanded the concessional loan program to support skill development, business scaling, marketing, and value chain participation for startup entrepreneurs. I have allocated Rs. 730 million to provide loans at three percent interest rate for this program.

Section 68.title: The “Bhagat Sarbajit Entrepreneurship Development Program” will be implemented to
Section 68.content: create employment and income opportunities by preserving traditional skills, arts, and occupations of the Dalit community. Production and marketing of the materials including gold, silver, bronze, copper, iron, leather, wood, and stone will be carried out by using modern technology. I have allocated Rs. 500 million for providing capital grants, concessional loans, and skill development training for this program.

Section 69.title: The bonded warehouse facility will be provided to the industries exporting gold and
Section 69.content: silver jewelry. Industries that receive a minimum of 50 percent of their export value as foreign currency in advance payment will be permitted to purchase an equivalent amount of gold and silver.

Section 70.title: Public services related to industry and business will be made simple, accessible, and
Section 70.content: technology-friendly. Arrangements will be made to carry out all procedures from company registration to exit through a single-window system.

Section 71.title: Industries with approval to establish new industry in Special Economic Zones and
Section 71.content: industrial areas will be exempted from the rent for the first three years. Monthly rent in Special Economic Zones will be reduced from Rs. 20 to Rs. 5 per square meter. Benefits equivalent to the industries in Special Economic Zones will be provided to the industries in industrial zones if they export more than thirty percent of their production.

Section 72.title: Companies developing industrial zones will be provided the same benefits as
Section 72.content: hydropower production companies, and industries established within these industrial zones will be provided the same benefits as industries in Special Economic Zones. The prescribed monthly rent for industrial zones will be reduced by 50 percent. I have allocated Rs. 1.55 billion for the construction of industrial infrastructure.

Section 73.title: Industries operating within the Kathmandu Valley will be encouraged to relocate to
Section 73.content: industrial zones outside the valley in order to control pollution in the capital region. I have made arrangements to provide land on lease free of cost, for such industries.

Section 74.title: Laws related to land acquisition and land holding limit will be reviewed. Provisions
Section 74.content: will be made to allow the purchase of land above the ceiling for industries, agricultural farms, and housing apartments. Arrangements will be made to allow the sale of housing and apartments which were built with approval but unsold due to land ceiling restrictions.

Section 75.title: Nepal will be developed as a premier destination for foreign direct investment.
Section 75.content: Investment promotion and double taxation avoidance agreements will be signed with potential countries for investment. Procedures for the inflow of foreign investment and profit repatriation will be simplified. Anchor investment policy will be adopted to attract foreign investment in national priority sectors.

Section 76.title: Legal reforms will be carried out to strengthen Public-Private Partnership. An
Section 76.content: automated one-stop service center will be established under the Investment Board. Provision of viability gap funding will be made to attract investment in the projects of the priority sector.

Section 77.title: The Investment Board will be mandated to manage resources, select projects, and
Section 77.content: implement them in line with the Public-Private Partnership concept at the federal level along with the provincial and local levels. A Public-Private Partnership Directorate will be established under the Investment Board for this purpose.

Section 78.title: Legal provisions will be made to allow foreign investors, multinational companies,
Section 78.content: international institutions, and their branches to lease buildings or apartments for office or residential use.

Section 79.title: Institutional capacity of the Investment Board will be strengthened. Within fiscal year
Section 79.content: 2025/26, project development agreements worth Rs. 700 billion with the private sector will be made, and the construction of projects worth Rs. 400 billion will be initiated. I have allocated Rs. 740 million to the Investment Board.

Section 80.title: Permission will be granted to Nepali entrepreneurs or companies to export semi
Section 80.content: processed materials and establish processing plants or sales branches abroad. To facilitate this, legal provisions will be made to permit investment in foreign countries up to 25 percent of their annual export earnings. A provision will be made requiring at least 50 percent of the profit earned from such a business to be repatriated back into the country. The responsibility for approving investments made abroad will be assigned to the Investment Board.

Section 81.title: Legal provisions will be made to allow Nepali citizens to receive sweat shares in return
Section 81.content: for providing technology or specialized knowledge or services to foreign companies.

Section 82.title: The Industrial Park in Damak, Jhapa will be constructed, operated and managed under
Section 82.content: the Public-Private-Partnership through the Investment Board. Modern industrial zones will be developed in Daiji (Kanchanpur), Naubasta (Banke), Lakshmipur (Dang), Motipur (Rupandehi), Shaktikhor (Chitwan), and Mayurdhap (Makwanpur) with private sector participation through the Investment Board. Special Economic Zones in Panchkhal and Simara will be operated in partnership with the private sector.

Section 83.title: An export strategy targeting products with comparative and competitive advantage will
Section 83.content: be adopted. Trade infrastructure development and technology transfer will be prioritized. “Make in Nepal and Made in Nepal” campaign will be conducted in collaboration with the private sector.

Section 84.title: The Integrated Check Post in Bhairahawa and the dry port in Timure, Rasuwa will be
Section 84.content: completed and brought into operation. Construction of a dry port in Dodhara-Chandani, Kanchanpur will be initiated.

Section 85.title: An inventory of identified mineral resources from the geological study, including
Section 85.content: petroleum, copper, iron, magnesium, phosphorite, quartz, and precious stones, will be prepared. Petroleum exploration in Dailekh will be completed, and commercial production will be commenced based on sample test reports. Petroleum exploration will be initiated in Palpa, Sunsari, and Dang. The feasibility study of rare earth metals will be carried out by selecting the capable researchers from the international community.

Section 86.title: An international conference will be organized in fiscal year 2025/26 with the
Section 86.content: participation of mining experts to assess the potential for exploration, production, and marketing of mineral-based products in Nepal.

Section 87.title: Private sector will be encouraged to participate in commercial production and
Section 87.content: marketing of natural and mineral-based products. Arrangements will be made for the extraction and processing of mineral and river-based construction materials found environmentally and economically viable through environmental impact assessments, for domestic use and export.

Section 88.title: Quality standards will be defined in line with international norms, and mutual
Section 88.content: recognition will be established with export destination countries. Standardization and certification of products manufactured in Nepal will be made systematic and of high quality. The law related to protection of intellectual property will be updated to reflect current needs.

Section 89.title: Facilitation for providing working capital loans in easy and accessible way to
Section 89.content: manufacturing, tourism, and construction industries, along with housing development companies will be done.

Section 90.title: Smooth supply of food grains and salt will be ensured in remote and hilly areas. Fuel
Section 90.content: storage capacity will be expanded to ensure a smooth supply. Arrangements will be made to blend bioethanol in order to control pollution and reduce petrol imports.

Section 91.title: Expansion of the Amlekhgunj-Lothar petroleum pipeline and construction of storage
Section 91.content: site will be initiated. Construction of the Siliguri-Charali cross-border petroleum pipeline and storage site will be initiated.

Section 92.title: Malpractices such as black marketing, monopolies, syndicates, and the creation of
Section 92.content: artificial shortages will be controlled to maintain a clean, competitive, and consumer- friendly market. Consumer court will be expanded to all provinces.

Section 93.title: I have allocated Rs. 10.14 billion to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies.

Section 94.title: Nepal will be branded as a safe and attractive tourist destination through the
Section 94.content: development of infrastructure, expansion of quality services, and marketing. Special promotional packages will be launched targeting tourists from the neighboring countries.

Section 95.title: Tourist-centric services will be expanded in major destinations of eco-tourism,
Section 95.content: mountain and adventure tourism, and religious and cultural tourism. Tourism promotion programs based on nature, culture, adventure, movies, wellness, and sports will be implemented. Welcome and Service Centers will be established at entry points targeting tourist arriving by land routes.

Section 96.title: Private sector investment will be encouraged in the development of tourism
Section 96.content: infrastructure. Development of jungle safari, trekking trails, and eco-tourism facilities in national parks, reserves, and protected areas will be emphasized. Arrangements will be made to lease the government-owned land, including forest areas for the construction of tourism infrastructure such as hill stations, hotels, lodges, and resorts.

Section 97.title: Tourism promotion programs will be conducted in collaboration with the private sector
Section 97.content: and with the facilitation from the Nepal Tourism Board. Safe and accessible trekking routes will be developed to promote tourism in the high hill and himalayan regions. Trekking routes will be operated along Shuklaphanta-Khaptad, Bardiya-Rara, Lumbini- Muktinath, Sauraha-Gosaikunda, Janakpurdham-Kalinchowk, Koshi Tappu- Sagarmatha, and Kechana-Pathibhara. Likewise, eco-tourism trails to Khaptad, Ramaroshan, Badimalika, Budhinanda, Rara, Swargadwari, and Muktinath will be developed. A reliable system for the safety and emergency rescue of trekkers and mountaineers will be arranged.

Section 98.title: Hotels and resorts will be granted income tax and electricity tariff exemptions
Section 98.content: equivalent to those provided to manufacturing industries. Legal provisions will be introduced to provide incentive through service charges to workers employed in tourism businesses such as hotels, motels, restaurants, and jungle safaris.

Section 99.title: Infrastructure will be developed at major religious, cultural, and tourism destinations
Section 99.content: such as Sagarmatha, Pashupatinath, Lumbini, Janakpurdham, Muktinath, Swargadwari, Rara, Khaptad. A comprehensive Lumbini Master Plan will be prepared and implemented for the protection, development, and promotion of the Lumbini area. Sandhyakalin Sampada Marga (Evening heritage trails) will be developed in Swayambhunath, Hanumandhoka, Pashupatinath, and Boudhanath areas.

Section 100.title: Development of tourism infrastructure will be emphasized in the attractive locations
Section 100.content: near the Pushpalal Mid-Hill Highway. Private sector will be encouraged to carry out rafting and other tourism activities in major rivers including Karnali, Bheri, Gandaki, Trishuli, Koshi.

Section 101.title: The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal will be strengthened institutionally by separating
Section 101.content: into regulatory and service providing agencies. Necessary measures will be taken to delist Nepal from aviation safety concern list within the upcoming fiscal year. Domestic aviation services will be made safer and more accessible.

Section 102.title: I have allocated Rs. 4.15 billion to develop the Tribhuvan International Airport into a
Section 102.content: boutique airport by expanding the capacity for managing the increasing passenger traffic. The Pokhara International Airport will be developed as a tourism hub.

Section 103.title: The Gautam Buddha International Airport will be operated with necessary facilities to
Section 103.content: make it cost-effective for tourists and migrant workers. Special incentives will be provided to operate cargo services from this airport.

Section 104.title: International airlines operating in Nepal will be encouraged to operate a fixed number
Section 104.content: of flights from Bhairahawa and Pokhara airports through additional facilities and incentives. The construction process of Nijgadh International Airport will be initiated through the use of alternative development financing.

Section 105.title: Capacity of Bhadrapur (Jhapa), Tarigaun (Dang), and Suketar (Taplejung) airports will
Section 105.content: be expanded. Pre-preparatory work for the construction of a regional airport in Surkhet will be completed, and constructions work will be initiated. Detailed project reports will be prepared for Chuhandanda (Tehrathum), Ajaymeru (Dadeldhura), and Sagarmatha (Udayapur) airports. I have allocated Rs. 500 million for the development of domestic airport infrastructure.

Section 106.title: Alternative utilization plans will be formulated for domestic airports with low traffic.
Section 106.content: Such airports will be used for aviation training and adventure tourism activities such as paragliding, parachuting, ultralight, skydiving in partnership with the private sector. Economic and commercial feasibility will be considered as the main criteria for the construction and expansion of new domestic airports.

Section 107.title: Ancient history, culture, and archaeological heritage of Nepal will be preserved. Panini
Section 107.content: Knowledge Park will be established in Panena, Arghakhanchi in the memory of Rishi Panini, the founder of Sanskrit grammar. I have allocated budget for digital archiving of historically and archaeologically significant documents.

Section 108.title: I have allocated Rs. 13.28 billion to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation.

Section 109.title: Forest areas will be conserved and forest products will be utilized as national resources.
Section 109.content: Forest areas will be utilized for commercial purposes and managed sustainably in a manner that does not adversely affect the environment and biodiversity.

Section 110.title: The provision requiring re-measurement before cutting down the trees that have been
Section 110.content: previously measured while granting the right to forest area uses will be removed. Withered and fallen trees will be collected and utilized.

Section 111.title: Seasoning industries will be encouraged to increase quality production and
Section 111.content: consumption of domestic wood and wood-based products. The establishment of Furniture and veneer industries will be encouraged in the vicinity of the Pushpalal Mid- Hill Highway.

Section 112.title: Grasslands and water sources will be managed to conserve biodiversity and natural
Section 112.content: habitats of wildlife. Community development, income generation, and employment programs will be implemented for residents of buffer zones. Buffer zones will be managed ensuring human-wildlife coexistence. Solar fencing with modern technology will be utilized for conservation and control of elephant’s natural corridors to prevent loss of life and property from wild elephant attacks.

Section 113.title: Export promotion of herbs will be emphasized by carrying out production, collection,
Section 113.content: processing, lab certification, and marketing. The production capacity of Herbs Production and Processing Company Limited will be enhanced by infrastructure development and improved management. I have allocated Rs. 200 million for this purpose.

Section 114.title: Communities will be encouraged to plant and conserve fruits, herbs, and high-value
Section 114.content: plants in the community forests and the sides of national highways. The Fruit Forest Program will be executed in collaboration with communities.

Section 115.title: Integrated watersheds management will be implemented to make water cycles
Section 115.content: sustainable in Chure and Terai-Madhesh regions. Conservation of gorges and wetlands, afforestation and natural restoration of forest, water retention and recharge related programs will be implemented. I have allocated Rs. 1.69 billion for these activities.

Section 116.title: National parks, conservation areas, and forest areas will be utilized, and development
Section 116.content: projects will be implemented without adversely affecting the environment and biodiversity. An arrangement will be made to deposit only one percent of the land management and tree nurturing costs into the Forest Development Fund for using forest areas in development projects implemented by the federal, provincial, and local levels.

Section 117.title: Environmental Impact Assessment process will be made swift, simple, and easy. A
Section 117.content: provision will be made to approve project site selection and environmental report simultaneously. A provision will be made to exempt supplementary environmental impact assessment after approval of the report if the number of trees to be cut increases by no more than ten percent or decreases.

Section 118.title: I have prohibited the production, import, sale, distribution, and use of plastic with a
Section 118.content: thickness of less than 40 microns effective from Mangsir 1, 2082 B.S. (November 17, 2025) to reduce the environmental pollution caused by plastic materials. I have provisioned capital grants to existing industries for replacement of dye to upgrade the quality of the product accordingly.

Section 119.title: Environmental Protection Programs will be implemented considering melting
Section 119.content: mountains, shrinking glaciers, and adverse impacts on the overall ecosystem. Nepal's interests will be advocated in international forums in line with the principle of climate justice. Financial access to climate funds will be enhanced. The declaration of the Sagarmatha Sambad will be implemented. Climate adaptation programs will be internalized up to the provincial and local levels in collaboration with the global community.

Section 120.title: Policy clarity will be established encompassing all aspects of carbon trade. Necessary
Section 120.content: preparations will be made to sell carbon credits at competitive price in international market through accurate accounting of carbon credits generated from emission reduction efforts.

Section 121.title: Priority will be given to public health and environment protection by implementing
Section 121.content: standards to control noise, air, and water pollution. The national air quality standard will be updated and implemented to reduce the effects of rising air pollution.

Section 122.title: Concessional loans will be provided to the private sector to replace traditional boilers
Section 122.content: used in factory with electric boilers in order to reduce air pollution in major cities of the country including the Kathmandu Valley.

Section 123.title: Awareness campaigns will be conducted at the community level to conserve
Section 123.content: biodiversity, and prevent and control forest fires. Individuals and communities who provide information about forest fire perpetrators to bring them under the purview of law, and assist in extinguishing forest fires will be rewarded.

Section 124.title: I have allocated Rs. 18.61 billion to the Ministry of Forests and Environment.

Section 125.title: Citizens' easy access to public information will be ensured. Transparency and
Section 125.content: accountability will be enhanced by promoting press freedom. The rights to personal freedom and privacy of citizens will be protected.

Section 126.title: Exploration, research, development, and innovation of the latest technologies
Section 126.content: developed in the field of communication and information technology will be emphasized. The second version of the Digital Nepal Framework will be formulated. Special programs on digital literacy will be conducted. I have allocated Rs. 740 million for the construction of digital infrastructure and development of the digital ecosystem.

Section 127.title: Partnerships with the private sector will be done for the construction, operation, and
Section 127.content: development of data center infrastructure. An Information Technology Park will be established in Kathmandu. Feasibility study will be conducted for establishing a data center in the Mid-Hill region to attract foreign investment in the information technology sector. Land, uninterrupted power supply, and security will be provided to domestic and foreign companies interested in setting up data centers.

Section 128.title: The Integrated Data Management Center will be upgraded. The capacity of the Disaster
Section 128.content: Recovery Center in Hetauda will be expanded, and the under-construction Data Center in Kohalpur will be brought into operation.

Section 129.title: Cloud infrastructure will be upgraded for reliable data security. The foundation will be
Section 129.content: laid for the establishment of Nepal's satellite in geostationary satellite orbit.

Section 130.title: An ecosystem for the information technology industry will be developed. Policy
Section 130.content: arrangements will be made to promote the export of information technology services.

Section 131.title: An AI Center will be established in collaboration with the private sector for research,
Section 131.content: application, and expansion of artificial intelligence and machine learning. Facilitation will be done to promote the commercial use of artificial intelligence.

Section 132.title: Private sector will be encouraged to build indoor and outdoor studios for filming
Section 132.content: domestic and international movies that reflect Nepal’s art, culture, civilization, and geographical diversity.

Section 133.title: The Nepal Telecommunications Authority will be restructured. Digital divide will be
Section 133.content: reduced by expanding access to information technology. Broadband services will be extended. The access and quality of 4G services will be improved throughout the country. 5G services will be launched in the Kathmandu Valley and major urban areas. I have made arrangements for IMEI registration to prevent illegal import and use of mobile sets.

Section 134.title: Standards for hardware and software will be developed to ensure uniformity in the
Section 134.content: information technology infrastructure of public agencies. Arrangements will be made for public agencies to prioritize the use of information technology software developed domestically.

Section 135.title: The NTV World Channel and PSB Digital Platform will be launched to expand the
Section 135.content: international reach of public service broadcasting. Legal arrangements will be made to regulate existing OTT services in telecommunications and broadcasting services. Advertising will be standardized, dignified, and organized.

Section 136.title: The use of social networks and digital platforms will be made dignified and organized.
Section 136.content: Necessary infrastructure and manpower will be developed to reduce cybersecurity risks. Security advisories will be issued quarterly by assessing cybersecurity risks.

Section 137.title: The infrastructure for the security printing center will be completed, and printing
Section 137.content: operations will be commenced. Interconnectivity will be established among postal- related agencies to expand e-commerce and operate logistics services. Post offices will be gradually developed into smart post offices.

Section 145.title: Workers' rights and interests will be protected by promoting dignified labor practices,

Section 146.title: All Nepali will be included in a life-cycle-based social security system. Individuals with

Section 148.title: It will be prohibited to top-up funds and duplicate benefits through similar programs
Section 148.content: from provinces and local levels for the social security programs run by the federal government. An integrated reporting system for social security benefits will be developed. I have allocated Rs. 109 billion for all categories of social security allowances.

Section 150.content: to enable individuals to shape their own future. The education system will be modernized and made technology-friendly.

Section 151.title: Incentive programs based on educational results will be implemented in 100 schools,
Section 151.content: ensuring at least one school in each district. Arrangements will be made for these schools to support other schools in improving their results. For this program, Rs. 2.5 million will be provided to each school.

Section 152.title: Schools will be re-mapped based on the number of teachers and students, geographic
Section 152.content: distance and transport facilities. School merger policy will be adopted based on this mapping. I have arranged incentive grants for the merged schools. The positions of teacher will be reviewed. Training will be arranged to enhance teachers' capacities on a periodical basis.

Section 153.title: Policies will be adopted for the improvement of results and quality of school education
Section 153.content: by expanding the scope of corporate social responsibility. Lesson learned from successful management practices of community and institutional schools will be applied to other community schools to improve their quality. A teacher bank will be established in cooperation with universities to prevent shortage of teachers in English, Science and Mathematics. Bachelor level graduates will be mobilized as volunteer teachers.

Section 154.title: Conditional grants in the education sector will gradually be converted into fiscal
Section 154.content: equalization grants. Arrangements will be made for the conduction and management of secondary education examinations by Provincial level.

Section 155.title: I have allocated Rs. 10.19 billion by increasing the budget for the Mid-Day Meal
Section 155.content: Program provided to students up to grade five. This will benefit 2.8 million students. I have allocated Rs. 1.29 billion to continue free sanitary pad distribution program in schools. This will benefit 1.3 million girl students.

Section 156.title: Scholarships being provided to students from targeted communities and remote
Section 156.content: mountainous districts will be continued. Incentive scholarship will be provided to students from the Musahar, Dom, and Chamar communities for higher education in the medical field. I have allocated Rs. 2.44 billion for this scholarship.

Section 157.title: I have increased the conditional grant being provided by the federal government for the
Section 157.content: remuneration of early childhood development support worker and school staff working in community schools. For this purpose, I have allocated Rs. 10.16 billion.

Section 158.title: A teaching-learning system based on Nepali originality will be developed. Virtual
Section 158.content: teaching system will be used in school education. Digital learning portal will be developed to enhance the quality of education. Hostels will be arranged to help students with disabilities to complete basic-level education. Schools, including private ones, will be effectively monitored by developing national regulatory standard.

Section 159.title: The subject-specific and methodological uniqueness of traditional education method
Section 159.content: including Gurukul, Gumba, and Madrasa will be preserved and promoted.

Section 160.title: Under the National Education Reform Program, capital grants will be provided for the
Section 160.content: construction of physical infrastructure of schools with more than 1,500 students in Terai-Madhesh, 1,000 in hills, and 500 in mountains. Ongoing construction of model schools will be completed. I have allocated Rs. 2.72 billion for this program.

Section 161.title: Higher education will be made research-oriented. Uniformity in the operation of
Section 161.content: universities will be maintained by formulating an umbrella act related to higher education. Emphasis will be given on reducing the trend of going abroad for studies and on developing human resources based on labor market demands. Departments and faculties of the universities will be restructured.

Section 162.title: The University Grants Commission will be restructured to develop it as a robust
Section 162.content: regulatory body for higher education. Grants will be provided to universities based on student numbers, academic quality, and infrastructure needs. Provisions will be made to publish academic calendars before the academic year begins, monitor their implementation, and withhold grants from universities that fail to comply the calendar.

Section 163.title: The infrastructure development and human resource management of the Madan
Section 163.content: Bhandari University of Science and Technology will be carried forward. The Shahid Dashrathchand Health Science University will be brought into operation. Infrastructure of the Vidushi Yogmaya Himalayan Ayurved University will be constructed.

Section 164.title: Policy will be adopted to attract foreign students as well to universities. Foreign
Section 164.content: students will be provided free visas for the duration of the academic calendar. Arrangement for multiple-entry visas will be made for their guardians.

Section 165.title: Scholarships will be provided to produce the necessary human resources for the public
Section 165.content: health system, based on subject and number. As per the recommendations of the High- Level Economic Reform Advisory Commission, scholarships provided in medical education will be targeted toward poor, meritorious, and students from extremely remote areas.

Section 166.title: I have allocated Rs. 560 million to initiate the construction of the infrastructure of
Section 166.content: medical colleges under construction and proposed in Bardibas, Butwal, Surkhet, and Dadeldhura.

Section 167.title: The study quotas will be increased by reviewing existing standards to prevent shortages
Section 167.content: of human resources in technical fields such as medicine, engineering, information technology, and nursing.

Section 168.title: Students who have completed school education will be encouraged to enroll in technical
Section 168.content: and vocational education or university education based on their results. Youths who are unable to get higher education will be made entrepreneurial through skill-based training. Training of more than six months will be provided to 26,900 youths through the Council for Technical Education and Vocational Training in the upcoming year.

Section 169.title: One technical school in each province will be selected and upgraded to a model
Section 169.content: educational institution. The provision will be made for the students from technical streams of general schools to be allowed to use the infrastructure and facilities of these educational institutions for skill development.

Section 170.title: Interns will be mobilized in public institutions based on the nature of service. Padhdai
Section 170.content: Kamaudai (Work while Studying) program will be implemented with 20 hours of work per week with a minimum wage to promote entrepreneurship-friendly education.

Disease-free Nepal: Healthy Nepali  172. ‘Nirogi Nepal’ (Disease-free Nepal) campaign will be launched to develop lifestyles with healthy diet, yoga, meditation, exercise, and positive thinking. Free, accessible, and quality basic health services will be provided to the general citizens. Investment will be increased in competent manpower, modern equipment, and infrastructure to expand the scope of specialized health services.

Section 173.title: The Health Insurance Program will be restructured. The legal provisions related to this
Section 173.content: program will be effectively implemented and its scope will be expanded. The benefit package for insured individuals will be increased gradually. The Social Health Security Program will be integrated into the health insurance. Insured individuals will be given the option to choose from different policies. Duplication will be eliminated, leakages will be controlled, and institutional governance will be maintained to prevent misuse of insurance facilities. Insurance benefits will be continued for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, Dalits, the ultra-poor, and minority communities. I have allocated Rs. 10 billion for the Health Insurance Program. Additionally, I have made arrangements to verify and settle the remaining claim payments through third-party assessment within this fiscal year.

Section 174.title: Specialized services equipped with skilled doctors and modern equipment will be
Section 174.content: expanded for the diagnosis and treatment of non-communicable diseases such as high blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, kidney disease, liver disease, and cancer. Treatment services for heart disease and cancer will be expanded in seven provinces. Arrangements will be made to conduct intensive screening for non-communicable diseases in the month of Falgun.

Section 175.title: Supply of medicines currently being provided free of charge from primary health
Section 175.content: service centers and primary hospitals will be ensured. Arrangements will be made to record and publish the data of the distributed medicines through website. I have allocated Rs. 2.06 billion for this purpose.

Section 176.title: I have allocated necessary budget to enhance preparedness and response to health
Section 176.content: emergencies arising from infectious diseases and pandemics, and to control vector- borne diseases such as dengue. Latest technologies will be adopted for the diagnosis and treatment of sickle cell anemia, a serious health issue in the Tharu community.

Section 177.title: Specialized burn treatment units will be operated in one government hospital in all
Section 177.content: provinces to provide quality burn treatment services within the country. An advanced intensive care unit for burn treatment will be expanded in the Bir Hospital.

Section 178.title: I have made arrangements for capital grants to improve the services and quality of the
Section 178.content: Kirtipur Burn Hospital, Dhulikhel Hospital, Kathmandu Institute of Child Health, Tilganga Eye Hospital, and Rana Ambika Eye Hospital.

Section 179.title: The ongoing construction of primary hospitals will be completed. Construction
Section 179.content: completed hospitals will be operated in collaboration with local levels and communities. I have allocated Rs. 11.24 billion for this purpose.

Section 180.title: Telemedicine and digital health services will be expanded to ensure easy access to
Section 180.content: health services for all citizens. Robotic technology and artificial intelligence will be used for ultra-modern health services.

Section 181.title: I have allocated budget for construction of infrastructure, equipment, and human
Section 181.content: resource management to provide international-standard medical education and ultra- modern health services at the Bir Hospital. The Kanti Children's Hospital will be developed as a center of excellence for child health services.

Section 182.title: The free testing program for cervical and breast cancer, as well as uterine prolapse, will
Section 182.content: be continued. I have allocated funds for the HPV vaccine targeted at young girls and free cancer treatment for children under the age of fourteen years.

Section 183.title: I have allocated Rs. 13.82 billion to operate the Safe Motherhood Program, the Golden
Section 183.content: Thousand Days Program, and the Social Health Security Program for indigent citizens to protect the lives of pregnant women, postpartum women, and newborns. Services for the identification, treatment, and rehabilitation for the children with autism and intellectual disabilities will be initiated in all provinces.

Section 184.title: Mental health problems will be eradicated through psychosocial counseling and
Section 184.content: awareness programs. The capacity of the Mental Hospital in Lagankhel will be expanded. National Neuroscience Center will be established in the central hospital located in the Kathmandu Valley to provide quality treatment for brain, spinal cord, and neurological disorders.

Section 185.title: The National Public Health Laboratory in Teku will be upgraded to an international-
Section 185.content: standard laboratory to make it capable of testing all types of samples by developing infrastructure, providing equipment, and managing human resources. I believe this will eliminate the need to send samples abroad for testing.

Section 186.title: Alternative treatment methods such as Ayurveda, naturopathy, homeopathy,
Section 186.content: acupuncture, Amchi will be promoted. The production capacity of Singhadurbar Vaidyakhana will be expanded. A National Ayurveda Panchakarma Yoga Service Center will be brought into operation. Nagarik Arogya Karyakram (Citizen Wellness Program) will be expanded to all local levels.

Section 187.title: Regulatory capacity will be strengthened to make quality medicines available at
Section 187.content: affordable prices. The quality of all types of medicines will be tested by expanding the capacity of National Drug Laboratory. Increasing the domestic production of essential medicines will be facilitated.

Section 188.title: Benefits of the demographic dividend will be utilized for development and prosperity
Section 188.content: through the implementation of the National Population Policy. Production and employment opportunities will be created in the rural economy to change the situation of ‘vikas ukalo chadne, manchhe oralo jharne’ (development moving uphill, people moving downhill). Policies will be adopted to manage migration and to ensure that the population growth rate does not fall below the replacement level.

Section 189.title: I have allocated Rs. 95.81 billion to the Ministry of Health and Population.

Section 190.title: Youth will be inspired to engage in nation-building with self-discipline and a spirit of
Section 190.content: service. Youth contribution in the country's economic and social development, and service delivery will be enhanced.

Section 191.title: National volunteer identity cards will be provided to the youths above the age of 16
Section 191.content: years based on certain criteria in coordination with the National Youth Council. They will be mobilized in education, health, social awareness, environment protection, and rescue, relief and rehabilitation during disasters by making them competent through training and instruction.

Section 192.title: Collateral-free concessional loans ranging from Rs. 200 thousand to Rs. 2 million at
Section 192.content: three percent interest rate will be provided to educated youth based on their educational qualifications, business registration, skill test certificates, and project proposals to make them entrepreneurial and self-employed.

Section 193.title: Investment will be gradually increased to construct sports infrastructure and enhance
Section 193.content: players’ professionalism. Regular training and competitions will be organized to foster a high morale of “Ma Jitna Sakchhu” (I can win) in players.

Section 194.title: Private sector will be attracted to invest in sports infrastructure to produce national and
Section 194.content: international level players, and promote sports competitions. Access to roads, drinking water, and electricity will be ensured for such sports infrastructure.

Section 195.title: A modern international-standard stadium capable of hosting all type of sports
Section 195.content: competition will be constructed in Damak, Jhapa. High-altitude sports stadiums will be constructed in Solukhumbu, Mustang, and Jumla to diversify sports genres and promote sports tourism.

Section 196.title: I have allocated Rs. 420 million for the construction of Mulpani Cricket Stadium in
Section 196.content: Kathmandu, Girija Prasad Koirala Stadium in Morang, Fapla Cricket Stadium in Kailali, and Siddhartha Cricket Stadium in Rupandehi. I have allocated Rs. 400 million to upgrade cricket stadium in Kirtipur. I have provisioned conditional grant to purchase the created assets of the Gautam Buddha Cricket Stadium in Chitwan based on the evaluation to be conducted by the Tribhuvan University Institute of Engineering. I have significantly increased the budget to build sports infrastructure.

Section 197.title: I have allocated Rs. 540 million to organize the Tenth National Sports Competition in
Section 197.content: Birendranagar, Surkhet. I have allocated necessary budget to operationalize the National Anti-Doping Agency.

Section 198.title: Nepali athletes who win medals in international sports competitions will be rewarded.
Section 198.content: Educational scholarships will be provided to these athletes and their children. I have continued the incentive allowances being provided to athletes and coaches.

Section 199.title: Women targeted training and practice programs will be conducted to increase women's
Section 199.content: participation in sports. Special arrangements of awards will be made for outstanding female athletes.

Section 200.title: I have allocated budget to operate sports academies in at least three schools in each
Section 200.content: province. Children and youth will be mobilized in social service and rescue activities by making them dutiful, disciplined, self-reliant, virtuous, and capable through scouts.

Section 201.title: I have allocated Rs. 6.08 billion to the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

Section 202.title: The role of women in all sectors of national life will be made effective. Emphasis will
Section 202.content: be given to ending gender discrimination, developing leadership capacity, and empowerment. Policy and structural reforms will be made to ensure 33 percent women participation in the executive level of the public sector.

Section 203.title: Effective programs will be conducted to ensure economic, social, and cultural rights to
Section 203.content: equality by ending all types of discrimination and oppression against women. The confidence and self-respect in women will be enhanced by improving the educational and economic status of women.

Section 204.title: Nutrition programs targeted to pregnant and postpartum women, and children will be
Section 204.content: conducted. I have allocated necessary fund for the National Women Upliftment Program to continue the work of free airlift for pregnant and postpartum women in remote areas whose lives are at risk.

Section 205.title: Employment and self-employment opportunities will be increased through promotion
Section 205.content: of women-targeted entrepreneurship. Arrangements will be made to waive fees for registering or renewing industries, businesses, or companies in the name of women. Capacity development programs will be conducted to link the labor and skills of housewives with small and cottage enterprises.

Section 206.title: The opportunities for education, health, nutrition, recreation, and social protection will
Section 206.content: be made available to guarantee constitutionally provided child rights and comprehensive development of children. Partnership with local levels will be made to build children’s parks.

Section 207.title: The street-children-free national campaign will be continued. Protection, family
Section 207.content: reunion, social rehabilitation, and alternative care arrangements will be made for abandoned, neglected, and parentless children. Capacity of the juvenile correction homes will be expanded. Psychosocial and career counseling will be made available to children involved in delinquency to bring them back to the right path. Child helpline service will be linked with the Nagarik (citizen) app.

Section 208.title: The knowledge, skills, and experience of senior citizens will be passed down through
Section 208.content: generations. Arrangements will be made for social security and health treatment to the senior citizens. Collaboration will be done with philanthropic organizations engaged in the street-human-free campaign for those in need.

Section 209.title: The identity card distribution system will be organized by updating the standards for
Section 209.content: identification and classification of persons with disabilities. Public services will be made disable-friendly. Community-based rehabilitation services will be expanded for helpless, incapacitated, and completely disabled persons.

Section 210.title: Programs for information gathering, monitoring, and awareness will be implemented
Section 210.content: to control the risk of human trafficking. Zero-tolerance policy will be adopted against all types of violence and oppression against women, including acid attacks.

Section 211.title: Construction work of the service center for women, children, and senior citizens will
Section 211.content: be completed. Rehabilitation centers for women victims of violence will be established in Madhesh, Sudurpaschim, and the Kathmandu Valley. I have allocated Rs. 620 million for this purpose.

Section 212.title: A national campaign against untouchability and discrimination will be conducted to

Section 325.title: Arrangements will be made to fill in KYC details once a year at one place by concerned
Section 325.content: individual and it will be linked to the national identity card. Arrangements will be made for digital access to institutions requiring KYC details.

Section 326.title: Credit flow to the private sector will be expanded to make the economy dynamic. The
Section 326.content: existing sectoral risk regime will be reviewed and credit flow for working capital will be facilitated.

Section 327.title: Neo Bank will be established within the fiscal year 2025/26. Rural economy will be
Section 327.content: developed by increasing access to bank and financial institutions in these areas. Digital, mobile, and branchless banking services will be expanded.

Section 328.title: The scope of property insurance will be expanded to protect against losses caused by
Section 328.content: natural calamities, disasters, and accidents. Insurance companies will be directed to expand their access to the rural areas. Cyber security insurance service will be operated. Section 329.title: Policy and structural arrangements will be made to mobilize private capital through
Section 329.content: green and sustainable development bonds, aligned with the concept of green taxonomy. Capital will be attracted from international markets by issuing local currency-linked bonds.

Section 330.title: Investment companies listed in the securities market, and other institutional investors
Section 330.content: will be facilitated to invest in equity, bonds, and other securities of nationally prioritized industries. Legal provisions will be made to enable the Employees Provident Fund, Citizen Investment Trust, and Social Security Fund to invest in private equity and venture capital.

Section 331.title: Secondary market trading of government bonds will be started. Arrangements will be
Section 331.content: made to allow Non-Resident Nepali to trade in the secondary market.

Section 332.title: An integrated system for interest subsidy on concessional loans will be implemented to
Section 332.content: increase production, employment, and self-employment opportunities in targeted areas.

Section 333.title: Institutional and internal control systems of microfinance institutions will be reformed.
Section 333.content: Provision of loans at concessional interest rates will be facilitated for the rehabilitation of problematic microfinance borrowers.

Section 334.title: Arrangements will be made to allow the operation of hedging services to attract foreign
Section 334.content: investment by managing foreign exchange risk.

Section 335.title: A law related to credit transactions will be formulated. Insolvency Act will be timely
Section 335.content: amended. Remittance inflow from banking channel and its investment in productive sector will be encouraged. All payments made by public entities will be linked to electronic system.

Section 336.title: Arrangements will be made to confiscate and deposit criminal assets such as intangible
Section 336.content: currencies like crypto and illegal foreign currencies into the consolidated fund. The process to freeze, control, and confiscate criminal assets will be made more effective.  Public Enterprises Management

Section 337.title: Competitiveness of public enterprises will be developed through management
Section 337.content: autonomy, technology transfer, and innovation. Appropriate methods such as restructuring, transformation into company, strategic partnership, and divestment will be adopted to improve the management of the public enterprises. A policy to retain land ownership under the Government of Nepal will be adopted while managing government investments of public enterprises.

Section 338.title: Closed and sick industries under the ownership of the Government of Nepal will be
Section 338.content: operated and managed by utilizing modern technology on the basis of appropriateness. The Dhaubadi Iron Company will be operated under Public-Private Partnership.

Section 339.title: The government investments will be managed by studying the current status and
Section 339.content: commercial feasibility of public enterprises including the Janakpur Cigarette Factory, Gorakhkali Rubber Industry, Butwal Yarn Factory, Nepal Metal Company, Nepal Orind and Magnesite, and Hetauda and Udayapur Cement Industries.
