Section 340.content: general public while maintaining the majority shareholding to the Government of Nepal. Policy of strategic partnership will be adopted for institutional strengthening of this company.

Section 341.title: The regulatory capacity of the Nepal Electricity Authority will be enhanced. A robust
Section 341.content: institutional arrangement will be established to separate the roles of electricity generation, transmission, and distribution.

Section 342.title: Transforming the Nepal Airlines Corporation into public company, implementing
Section 342.content: management contracts and strategic partnerships with competent international airlines will be carried out to enhance its capacity, improve quality, and promote professionalism. Section 343.title: I have made arrangement to restrict - officials and employees of public enterprises that

Governance Reform and Corruption Control

Section 344.content: and local levels, as enshrined in the constitution, will be reviewed. Reforms will be made in prevailing laws to ensure functional alignment and uniformity in laws of all three levels. Policy, legal, and institutional reforms will be carried out under the guidance of the High-Level Governance Reform Commission.

Section 345.title: The Federal Civil Service Bill will be passed during the current parliamentary session.
Section 345.content: I believe this will establish uniformity in service conditions of civil servants and ensure their career development.

Section 346.title: The Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers will be developed as a Centre
Section 346.content: of Excellence to enhance public service effectiveness and make development result- oriented.

Section 347.content: in public service. Capacity of the Nagarik App will be expanded. Public service will be made simple, accessible, and cost-effective by integrating it into the Nagarik App. Arrangement will be made to securely store all government electronic data under a unified system.

Section 348.title: Optimum utilization of information technology will be done to make public service
Section 348.content: delivery simple, accessible and of high quality. Section 349.title: Although the need to update the benefits of public servants in a timely manner is well
Section 349.content: recognized, it has not been possible to increase salaries as expected due to pressure on resource management. Nevertheless, I have raised the monthly dearness allowance to Rs. 5 thousand for all public servants, effective from 1st Shrawan 2082 (mid-July 2025).

Section 350.title: Sulav Awas Karyakram (Affordable Housing Program) will be implemented through
Section 350.content: the initiatives of the retirement funds including Employees Provident Fund and participation from the private sector. Section 351.title: The Civil Service Hospital will be upgraded. The health care facilities currently being
Section 351.content: provided by the Employees Provident Fund to contributors and their spouses will be expanded to other family members as well.

Section 352.title: Employees in the contract service within approved positions, as well as temporary and
Section 352.content: relief teachers, will be included in the contribution based social security scheme. Separate package with ten percent contribution from both employer and contributor will be developed and implemented for this purpose.

Section 353.content: resource. Transparency, accountability, and integrity will be maintained in performance of public institutions. Codes of conduct on professional ethics and discipline will be developed and implemented in public institutions. Continuous monitoring and supervision will be carried out in public institutions. Zero-tolerance against corruption will be adopted. Law on conflict of interest will be formulated. The second national strategy and action plan against corruption will be implemented.

Section 354.title: The Voter Identity Card will be integrated with the National Identity Card to enhance
Section 354.content: the credibility of elections. This initiative will be launched from the Kathmandu Valley.  Foreign Aid Mobilization

Section 355.title: In accordance with the Foreign Aid Mobilization Policy, 2025, assistance will be
Section 355.content: mobilized in projects that yield high returns in line with national needs and priorities. The country's leadership and ownership will be established in selection and implementation of projects. The capacity to utilize foreign aid will be enhanced.

Section 356.title: Assistance will be received in projects and programs that have completed preparation
Section 356.content: as per the project readiness filter. Implementation framework will be finalized to complete the project within the stipulated time and cost.

Section 357.title: Arrangements will be made to grant approval for the use of forest areas considering the
Section 357.content: projects implemented with foreign assistance as national priority projects. I expect this to speed up the implementation of projects.

Section 358.title: Assistance will be mobilized through co-investment from more than one donor agency
Section 358.content: for high-cost infrastructure projects including Dudhkoshi and Upper Arun based on economic feasibility.  Public Finance and Project Management

Section 359.title: The effectiveness of public finance will be increased by maintaining allocative
Section 359.content: efficiency. The outcomes of public expenditure will be increased through budget discipline. Cash flow management will be strengthened to balance the federal consolidated fund. Productive utilization and sustainability of public debt will be ensured. The national financial management reform strategy will be implemented.

Section 360.title: It has become indispensable to adopt innovative and successful practices of the
Section 360.content: international community to meet the need for development finance. Alternative Development Finance Bill has already been presented in the federal parliament to establish a legal framework for this purpose. I believe that this bill will be passed from the current session. I believe that this will attract both domestic and foreign private investment in the construction and operation of infrastructure projects of hydropower, solar energy, transmission lines, roads, tunnels, airports, urban infrastructure, tourism, and industrial infrastructure, foster long-term capital formation, and bring about qualitative changes in project construction and management. Construction of infrastructure projects will be commenced through alternative development finance in the upcoming fiscal year.

Section 361.title: Clear criteria will be developed for the selection of national pride projects. Existing
Section 361.content: national pride projects will be reviewed.

Section 362.title: I have streamlined project management through the reduction of number of
Section 362.content: development projects by 4,654 compared to the previous year. I have implemented a standard under which the federal government will not allocate less than Rs. 30 million to any new infrastructure project it undertakes. I have expected that this will help in resource management for national pride and priority projects and effectiveness of project implementation. The line ministries will be made more responsible to increase capital expenditure by improving budget execution capacity.

Section 363.title: Arrangements will be made to move projects into the procurement process that have
Section 363.content: completed preparations, such as land acquisition, forest area approval. Provisions will be made in the contract agreement to conduct the work in three shifts for accelerating project implementation.

Section 364.content: the specified time, projected cost, and quality. The electronic procurement system will be upgraded. Arrangements will be made to include all project-related works in a single contract package. Mediation process will be made legally compliant, transparent, and accountable for resolving disputes during the implementation of contract agreement.

Section 365.title: I have made arrangements for the province and local levels to formulate balanced
Section 365.content: budgets and manage multi-year liabilities within the limits of the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework.

Section 367.content: funds allocated for national pride and high-priority projects to other projects or programs, except in special circumstances. National dashboard system will be developed to monitor goal progress, quality, and timeframe for projects costing more than Rs. 250 million.

Section 368.content: decisions on time during project implementation. For projects with more than 80 percent progress, their completion will not be hindered due to shortage of resources.

Section 369.title: Emphasis will be given on achieving development results by completing the ongoing
Section 369.content: projects. I have allocated necessary funds for multi-year projects with assured resources and for the payment of liabilities incurred.

Section 370.content: specifications will be held accountable and brought under the purview of the law. Regional and local roads, other than national highways, will be constructed with intermediate lanes in hilly and mountainous areas.  Cost-effectiveness

Section 371.title: Laws will be developed to strengthen budget discipline as specified in the constitution
Section 371.content: at the federation, province, and local levels. Public expenditure standards applicable to all three levels will be formulated.

Section 375.title: I have made arrangements for citizens who have completed 70 years of age to receive
Section 375.content: senior citizen allowance from the upcoming fiscal year taking into account the report of the High-Level Economic Reforms and Suggestions Commission. I have kept the age requirement unchanged for the senior citizens in remote areas and targeted groups who are currently receiving the allowance.

Section 376.title: An umbrella law will be formulated to maintain uniformity in the operation and
Section 376.content: management of all Academies across the country. I have made arrangements for the Academies and development committees to operate and manage their liabilities within the limits of the current and capital grants available from the federal government.

Section 377.title: Foreign travel will not be undertaken at the expense of the Government of Nepal, except
Section 377.content: for high-level diplomatic visits, and mandatory representation in international organizations of which Nepal is a member.

I have made arrangements to prohibit consultancy services for drafting the documents such as laws, rules, policies, procedures, standards.

Section 379.content: contingency fund limit will be reduced up to 3 percent for projects with a cost estimate of up to Rs. 1 billion, and up to 2 percent for projects exceeding that amount.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson  Now, please allow me to present the budget allocation and resource management estimates for the implementation of the aforementioned sectoral policies and programs.

Section 380.title: I have allocated total expenditure of Rs. 1,964.11 billion for the upcoming fiscal year.
Section 380.content: Out of the total allocation, Rs. 1,180.98 billion, i.e., 60.1 percent, is allocated for recurrent expenditure, Rs. 407.89 billion, i.e., 20.8 percent, is for capital expenditure, and Rs. 375.24 billion, i.e., 19.1 percent, is for financing. This estimation is 5.6 percent higher than the current fiscal year's allocation and 18.2 percent higher than the revised estimates. Out of the total allocation, I have allocated Rs. 417.83 billion for fiscal transfers to province and local levels.

Section 381.title: Of the total estimated financing sources for the upcoming fiscal year, Rs. 1,315 billion
Section 381.content: will be financed through revenue mobilization and Rs. 53.45 billion from foreign grants, resulting a deficit of Rs. 595.66 billion. The net remaining amount of Rs. 362 billion after revenue and foreign aid mobilization will be financed from domestic borrowings.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson  Now, please allow me to present the revenue policy and programs for the fiscal year 2025/26.

Section 382.title: It is necessary to make the revenue system investment-friendly and production-oriented
Section 382.content: and to manage resources for the ever-increasing public expenditure. It is necessary to attract foreign capital and technology by making the tax system compatible with international standards and practices. It is necessary to make revenue collection effective by improving tax compliance and controlling revenue leakage. Therefore, I have set the following objectives for the upcoming fiscal year to increase the productivity of the revenue system. (a) To broaden the tax base by encouraging economic activity, (b) To increase voluntary tax compliance by timely reform and simplification of tax laws, (c) To develop taxpayer-friendly, transparent, and automated revenue system, (d) To control revenue leakage by enhancing the efficiency of revenue administration, (e) To mobilize non-tax revenue while making the use of natural resources sustainable and cost-effective. Now, I present the programs related to revenue for the fiscal year 2025/26.  Timely Reforms in Tax Laws

Section 383.content: address changes in the tax system and new business models at the international level.

Section 384.title: A study will be conducted on relevance, and practical application of multiple rates of
Section 384.content: Value Added Tax, also considering the suggestions received for it.

Section 385.title: The rates of non-tax revenue will be updated by amending the sectoral laws.

Section 388.content: 100 million from income tax for 5 years.

Section 392.content: equipment to be imported for the green hydrogen producing industry. I have made arrangements to provide income tax exemption to green hydrogen producers for 5 years.

Section 393.title: I have made arrangements to levy 1 percent customs duty and exempt other taxes and

Section 396.title: I have made arrangements to levy 1 percent customs duty and exempt the remaining
Section 396.content: taxes and duties while importing tunnel boring machines by the private sector to promote the use of tunneling technology in road, irrigation, and hydropower projects.

Section 397.title: I have made arrangements allowing freight service providers to deduct the amount paid
Section 397.content: as fare for means of transportation owned by a natural person, on which advance tax has been withheld when calculating taxable income.

Section 398.title: I have made a provision requiring mandatory affiliation of retirement funds previously
Section 398.content: approved by the Inland Revenue Department with retirement funds operated by the Employees Provident Fund, Citizen Investment Trust, Social Security Fund, or Pension Fund.

Section 399.title: I have provided concessions on interest, additional fees, late fees, and penalties to those
Section 399.content: who have failed to submit their Value Added Tax and Excise Duty returns or to pay taxes if they submit their returns and taxes.

Section 400.content: aviation service providers and their air ticket sellers register for Value Added Tax and pay the outstanding tax amount.

Section 401.content: returns to settle the arrears created by the amended tax assessment done by the office.

Section 402.title: I have abolished the Value-Added Tax levied on clearing house services to encourage

Section 403.content: as food grains, beans, fruits, as well as animal and dairy products.

Section 405.content: land to bring in up to US dollar 5 thousand or equivalent in travelers’ cheque and other foreign currency for exchange within Nepal; any amount exceeding this limit must be declared at the customs checkpoint.

Section 406.title: I have removed the existing price limit of Rs. 1.6 million on ambulances carrying
Section 406.content: patients that can be imported under the revenue exemption facility.

Section 407.title: To reduce environment pollution by encouraging the use of electric vehicles and to
Section 407.content: increase domestic consumption of electricity, I have maintained all taxes and duties levied on such vehicles as it is.  Broadening of the Tax Scope and Base Protection

Section 408.title: I have increased the customs duty rate on the import of alcohol, beer, tobacco, and
Section 408.content: cigarettes. I have adjusted some of the customs duty rates. I have made a modest increase in the existing excise duty rate. I have expanded the scope of the health risk tax.

Section 409.title: The scope of the central billing monitoring system will be expanded while increasing
Section 409.content: taxpayer participation in the electronic billing system.

Section 410.title: Voluntary tax participation will be enhanced through taxpayer education and

Section 411.title: I have expanded the scope of the Digital Service Tax to bring all types of digital
Section 411.content: transactions under the purview of taxation.

Section 412.title: The tax expenditure system will be made rational by timely revision of tax exemptions,
Section 412.content: concessions, and facilities.  Trade Facilitation and Improvement in Service Delivery

Section 413.title: I have made a provision that prohibits the collection of entry fees, route charges, or any
Section 413.content: other duties by the federation, province, or local levels on temporary imported vehicles, means of transportation, and equipment after customs duties have been collected at the customs points while transporting within Nepal.

Section 414.title: I have abolished the provision of bank guarantee of Rs. 300 thousand to be provided by
Section 414.content: industrialists and businessmen engaged in export and import while obtaining EXIM code.

Section 415.title: I have repealed the existing provision that requires the taxpayers to pay minimum tax
Section 415.content: even if they have not made any taxable transactions.

Section 416.content: with fast-track clearance facilities and on-site inspection services for goods during import and export.

Section 417.content: trends will be developed, and the reference value will be replaced by an automated valuation system.  Control of Revenue leakage

Section 418.content: data and information related to bilateral trade with neighboring countries.

Section 419.content: leakage. Information exchange and joint monitoring among agencies involved in revenue mobilization will be made effective.  Increasing Efficiency in Revenue Administration

Section 420.content: faceless system by specializing, and enhancing the capacity and efficiency of revenue administration.

Section 421.title: Integrated check points will be established and upgraded at major custom points to
Section 421.content: facilitate trade and reduce business costs.

Section 422.title: Business Process Reengineering will be carried out to make timely changes in the
Section 422.content: inland revenue information system. I believe that this will simplify the work process and tax compliance, and reduce collection cost.

Section 423.content: and Modernization Action Plan will be accelerated.

Section 424.title: Foreign trade will be facilitated by expanding the scope of the national single window
Section 424.content: information system.  Right Honourable Speaker, Right Honourable Chairperson

Section 425.title: I have presented the actual expenditure for last fiscal year 2023/24, the revised estimate

Section 426.title: I expect that economic reforms will be paced and a conducive environment will be
Section 426.content: created to achieve high and sustainable economic growth from the execution of the proposed budget. I believe this will bring dynamism in the economy and acceleration in development.
